sources.entry: Plannotator by backnotprop - Interactive review UI that intercepts ExitPlanMode via hooks, letting you visually annotate plans with comments, deletions, and replacements before approving or denying with detailed feedback. Has since grown to cover code and diff review, PRs, and rendered HTML artifacts, with feedback sent straight back to the agent. Supports several coding agents alongside Claude Co

summary.one_liner: Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface that lets you annotate plans, markdown, HTML, diffs and PRs from AI coding agents and send feedback back to the agent.
summary.what_it_does: Plannotator runs a local server and opens a review UI in your browser when an AI coding agent proposes a plan, writes HTML or finishes code. You can comment on, delete or replace text in plans and markdown, annotate rendered HTML, and review local diffs or GitHub/GitLab PRs and MRs with a diff viewer and file tree. Approving or denying a plan, or sending review comments, returns structured feedback to the agent session. The README describes support for Git, GitButler, Jujutsu, Perforce, GitHub and GitLab, plus an optional Inbox where agents leave messages and questions. Sharing, Ask AI and review agents are optional features with separate network behavior documented in the README.
use_cases: review an AI agent's plan before it starts coding
annotate markdown specs and send comments back to the agent
review uncommitted changes or a pull request in a browser diff viewer
approve or deny a plan with written feedback
annotate HTML reports generated by an agent
share a plan with a teammate for annotation
notable: Intercepts Claude Code's ExitPlanMode via a PermissionRequest hook so plans open for review before implementation
Supports many agents including Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Amp and Pi
Code review covers local changes and remote GitHub PRs and GitLab MRs, with line comments and file staging
Share links encrypt large payloads with AES-256-GCM, and the paste service is self-hostable
Release binaries ship with SHA256 sidecars, SLSA provenance and an SBOM
caveats: Sends content to outside services in some cases: URL annotation uses Jina Reader by default, and Ask AI sends context to your configured provider
Performs a GitHub release check when review surfaces load, with no opt-out setting for that check
Legacy open source link sharing is deprecated; Workspaces is a separate hosted product
Droid has commands only, with no plan interception yet; native Windows Codex hooks are experimental
